49089-recollections-of-a-pioneer.creator: Unknown
49089-recollections-of-a-pioneer.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. I was born in Bartow County, Georgia, on the 22nd day of January, 1829. Sometime during my infancy, and at a period too early to be remembered, my father and his family moved to East Tennessee, where we lived until I was ten years old. About this time reports concerning the Platte Purchase and its splendid farming land began to reach us.

73651-modern-shipbuilding-and-the-men-en.description: A book by David Pollock,. ring during recent years, and the substantial progress, both in science and practice, which has marked the period, have often formed the subject of articles in the technical and daily press, and of papers read before professional institutions. So far as I am aware, however, no single work dealing historically with modern shipbuilding in a way at once trustworthy and popular, and in a form handy and accessible, has yet been published. arxiv-1811-06494.title: Large-Scale Distributed Algorithms for Facility Location with Outliers
arxiv-1811-06494.creator: Tanmay Inamdar, Shreyas Pai, Sriram V. Pemmaraju
arxiv-1811-06494.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Tanmay Inamdar, Shreyas Pai, Sriram V. Pemmaraju. This paper presents fast, distributed, O ⁡ ( 1 ) O(1) -approximation algorithms for metric facility location problems with outliers in the Congested Clique model, Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) model, and in the k k -machine model. The paper considers Robust Facility Location and Facility Location with Penalties , two versions of the facility location problem with outliers proposed by Charikar et al.

arxiv-2210-06957.title: Noether supercurrent operator mixing from lattice perturbation theory
arxiv-2210-06957.creator: G. Bergner, H. Panagopoulos, I. Soler, G. Spanoudes
arxiv-2210-06957.description: Abstract In this work we present perturbative results for the renormalization of the supercurrent operator, S μ S_{\mu} , in 𝒩 = 1 {\cal N}=1 Supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory. At the quantum level, this operator mixes with both gauge invariant and noninvariant operators, which have the same global transformation properties.

arxiv-2305-10005.title: DinoSR: Self-Distillation and Online Clustering for Self-supervised Speech Representation Learning
arxiv-2305-10005.creator: Alexander H. Liu, Heng-Jui Chang, Michael Auli, Wei-Ning Hsu, James Glass
arxiv-2305-10005.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce self- di stillatio n and o nline clustering for self-supervised s peech r epresentation learning (DinoSR) which combines masked language modeling, self-distillation, and online clustering. We show that these concepts complement each other and result in a strong representation learning model for speech.

arxiv-2412-02892.title: On the biautomaticity of CAT(0) triangle-square groups
arxiv-2412-02892.creator: Mateusz Kandybo
arxiv-2412-02892.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mateusz Kandybo. Following the research from the paper ‘‘Triangles, squares and geodesics’’ of Rena Levitt and Jon McCammond we investigate the properties of groups acting on CAT(0) triangle-square complexes, focusing mostly on biautomaticity of such groups. In particular we show two examples of nonpositively curved triangle-square complexes X 1 X_{1} and X 2 X_{2} , such that their universal covers violate conjectures given in the aforementioned paper.

arxiv-2503-22992.title: Evaluation of Remote Driver Performance in Urban Environment Operational Design Domains
arxiv-2503-22992.creator: OLE HANS, BENEDIKT WALTER, JÜRGEN ADAMY
arxiv-2503-22992.description: Abstract Remote driving has emerged as a solution for enabling human intervention in scenarios where Automated Driving Systems (ADS) face challenges, particularly in urban Operational Design Domains (ODDs). This study evaluates the performance of Remote Drivers (RDs) of passenger cars in a representative urban ODD in Las Vegas, focusing on the influence of cumulative driving experience and targeted training approaches.

arxiv-2504-19085.title: Toward Inclusive Low-Code Development: Detecting Accessibility Issues in User Reviews Conference: EASE 2025; June 17-20, 2025; Istanbul, Turkey ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in accessibility
arxiv-2504-19085.creator: Mohammadali Mohammadkhani, Sara Zahedi Movahed, Hourieh Khalajzadeh, Mojtaba Shahin, Khuong Tran Hoang
arxiv-2504-19085.description: Abstract . Low-code applications are gaining popularity across various fields, enabling non-developers to participate in the software development process. However, due to the strong reliance on graphical user interfaces, they may unintentionally exclude users with visual impairments, such as color blindness and low vision. This paper investigates the accessibility issues users report when using low-code applications.

pmc-11415005.title: Hepatorenal Syndrome in the Setting of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma and Chronic Lymphedema: A Case Report
pmc-11415005.creator: Sean Lief, Mohammed A Khan, Axel B Lichtenberg, Srihita Patibandla, Ali Z Ansari
pmc-11415005.description: Cholangiocarcinomas are aggressive cancers originating in the bile ducts, classified based on their location as intrahepatic, perihilar, or distal, and often present with symptoms such as jaundice, abdominal pain, and weight loss. Hepatorenal syndrome, a severe complication of liver failure that impairs kidney function and worsens prognosis, further complicates the management of these tumors.

pmc-11425600.title: Recent Advances in Metal Oxide and Phosphate Nanomaterials Radiolabeling with Medicinal Nuclides
pmc-11425600.creator: Tereza Janská, Michal Sakmár, Matěj Štíbr, Martin Vlk, Ján Kozempel
pmc-11425600.description: The utilization of nanomaterials in biomedical applications has surged in recent years; yet, the transition from research to practical implementation remains a great challenge. However, a promising area of research has emerged with the integration of nanomaterials with diagnostic and therapeutic radionuclides.

pmc-11462708.title: The utilization of N-acetylgalactosamine and its effect on the metabolism of amino acids in Erysipelotrichaceae strain
pmc-11462708.creator: Mengqing Zhou, Jinyuan Wu, Lin Wu, Xiao Sun, Congying Chen, Lusheng Huang
pmc-11462708.description: BackgroundThe metabolism of gut microbiota produces bioactive metabolites that modulate host physiology and promote self-growth. Erysipelotrichaceae is one of the most common anaerobic microorganism families in the gut, which has been discovered to play a vital role in host metabolic disorders and inflammatory diseases.

pmc-12563516.title: The Autoimmune Gastritis Puzzle: Emerging Cellular Crosstalk and Molecular Pathways Driving Parietal Cell Loss and ECL Cell Hyperplasia
pmc-12563516.creator: Sara Massironi, Elena Oriani, Giuseppe Dell’Anna, Silvio Danese, Federica Facciotti
pmc-12563516.description: Autoimmune gastritis (AIG) is a chronic, organ-specific autoimmune disease characterized by progressive destruction of gastric parietal cells driven by autoreactive CD4+ T-cells, epithelial stress pathways, and microbial factors. Parietal cell loss results in achlorhydria, intrinsic factor deficiency, and vitamin B12 malabsorption, ultimately leading to pernicious anemia.

pmc-13195714.title: CRISPR spacer profiling and prophage mining reveal diverse bacteriophages associated with Streptococcus Mutans
pmc-13195714.creator: Xiaolin Chen, Mingrui Zhang, Liuchang Yang, Yuxing Chen, Yaqi Chi, Yiran Zhao, Zhe Ma, Yongliang Li, Xiaoyan Wang
pmc-13195714.description: BackgroundStreptococcus mutans is a key cariogenic bacterium. Current antimicrobials lack species specificity, while phage-based approaches remain experimental and require more S. mutans phage isolates.ObjectiveTo profile the diversity of S. mutans-associated phages and strain-level heterogeneity in phage exposure using genome-informed CRISPR spacer and prophage analyses.Materials and methodsWe compiled 944 publicly available S. mutans genomes and dereplicated them into 735 non-redundant strains.

pmc-13459429.title: The relationship between school belonging and college students’ mental health: a chain mediation model involving physical exercise and a growth mindset
pmc-13459429.creator: Yong Jiang, Wei Jin, Beier Zhang
pmc-13459429.description: ObjectiveThis cross-sectional study examined the association between school belonging and symptom-based mental health among college students and tested whether physical exercise and growth mindset statistically mediated this association.MethodsA cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted among 600 college students. Mediation analysis was performed using the PROCESS macro (Model 6), and 95% confidence intervals were constructed using 5,000 bootstrap repetitions (bias-corrected percentile bootstrap).
